# hosttracker_monitor (Resource)

A HostTracker monitor: one check of one address, run on a schedule from the monitoring locations you choose.

Every optional attribute is also computed, because the API reads an absent member as "leave this alone" rather than as "clear this". Removing an attribute from the configuration therefore keeps the value it last had; to clear one, write the empty value (`""`, `[]`) explicitly.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An http monitor with a keyword check, run from everywhere, that needs
# every location to agree before it calls the site down.
resource "hosttracker_monitor" "marketing" {
  type     = "http"
  url      = "https://example.com/"
  name     = "Marketing site"
  interval = 300
  tags     = ["prod", "web"]

  locations = {
    pools    = ["allworld"]
    fallback = "world"
  }

  recheck = {
    strategy = "fullAgreement"
  }

  settings = {
    http = {
      method          = "G"
      keywords        = "Sign in"
      keyword_mode    = "PresentAny"
      follow_redirect = true
      timeout         = 20000

      headers = [
        {
          name  = "X-Monitored-By"
          value = "terraform"
        },
      ]

      # Sub-checks that ride on this monitor rather than costing a monitor
      # of their own.
      attached = {
        ssl_exp = { enabled = true }
        dnsbl   = { enabled = true }
      }

      cert_watch_days = [7, 30]
    }
  }
}

# A ping monitor pinned to European locations.
resource "hosttracker_monitor" "gateway" {
  type = "ping"
  url  = "gateway.example.com"
  name = "Edge gateway"

  locations = {
    pools = ["europe"]
  }
}

# A certificate-expiry monitor. It runs on the fixed internal network, so
# it takes no locations and its settings block has no members.
resource "hosttracker_monitor" "certificate" {
  type = "sslExp"
  url  = "https://example.com/"
  name = "Certificate"
}

# A type this provider has no typed settings block for yet, written
# through the JSON escape hatch. Only the members named here are managed.
resource "hosttracker_monitor" "api_check" {
  type = "api"
  url  = "https://example.com/health"
  name = "Health endpoint"

  locations = {
    pools = ["allworld"]
  }

  settings_json = jsonencode({
    method  = "G"
    accept  = "application/json"
    timeout = 15000
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `type` (String) Which kind of check this is: `http`, `waterfall`, `ping`, `port`, `domainExp`, `sslExp`, `dnsbl`, `webRisk`, `counter`, `cntCheck`, `api`, `database`, `snmp` or `tran`. The vocabulary is open, so a type newer than this provider is accepted too. `pageSpeed` is an accepted spelling of `waterfall`. The type cannot change after creation: editing it replaces the monitor.
- `url` (String) The address the check is aimed at: an absolute http(s) url for the types that fetch one, a bare host or address for the types that do not. It is stored raw and read back unchanged; `effective_url` carries what is actually monitored.

### Optional

- `cron_schedule` (String) A cron expression, replacing the fixed interval. Not accepted by the fixed-cadence types (blacklist, certificate and domain expiry, web risk).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the check runs. This is the configured flag, not the effective one: a monitor suspended by a package limit still reads `true` here and `paused` in `state`.
- `full_log` (Boolean) Record every check rather than only the state changes.
- `interval` (Number) How often the check runs, in seconds. Types that publish a fixed cadence schedule themselves and ignore it; the rest fall back to the account's default. The floor is per type and per package - read it from the `hosttracker_monitor_types` data source.
- `locations` (Attributes) Where the check runs from. The types that run on the fixed internal network (`dnsbl`, `sslExp`, `domainExp`, `webRisk`) refuse it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--locations))
- `name` (String) A display name. Never an identifier.
- `on_overlimit` (String) What to do when the account's package will not fit this monitor: `fail` (the default) refuses the write, `disable` creates it switched off with a package-limit reason. It is a knob on the write, not a stored member, so it is never read back. Pair `disable` with `enabled = false`: a monitor the API switches off while the configuration asks for `enabled = true` is a state Terraform reports as an inconsistent apply.
- `open_stat` (Boolean) Make this monitor's statistics publicly readable - the switch behind the public stats page and the uptime badge.
- `recheck` (Attributes) The quorum rule applied before a failure concludes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--recheck))
- `settings` (Attributes) The type-specific settings, as one block per monitor type. Fill in the block that matches `type` and leave the rest out. A type without a block of its own is written through `settings_json`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings))
- `settings_json` (String) The settings object as raw JSON, for a monitor type this provider has no typed block for yet. Mutually exclusive with `settings`. Only the members this attribute names are managed: the rest of the stored settings are left alone, and drift is reported for the named members only.
- `sla_target` (Number) The uptime percentage this monitor is measured against.
- `tags` (Set of String) Free-form labels. Writing this attribute replaces the whole set.

### Read-Only

- `created` (Number) When the monitor was created, in Unix seconds.
- `effective_url` (String) The normalized address actually monitored. Equal to `url` unless the API canonicalized it.
- `id` (String) The monitor's id.
- `since` (Number) When the current state began, in Unix seconds.
- `state` (String) The monitor's current state: `up`, `down`, `paused` or `maintenance`.
- `updated` (Number) The API's change marker, in Unix seconds. It moves on creation, on an up/down transition and on an automatic package-limit disable - not on a configuration edit.

<a id="nestedatt--locations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `locations`

Optional:

- `excluded_agents` (Set of String) Ids of monitoring locations to keep this check off.
- `fallback` (String) What happens when no location in the chosen pools is available: `geo`, `world` or `starve`.
- `pools` (Set of String) The monitoring-location pools to run from - at least one. `["allworld"]` means everywhere. Read the available pools from the `hosttracker_locations` data source.


<a id="nestedatt--recheck"></a>
### Nested Schema for `recheck`

Optional:

- `min_num_down` (Number) How many locations must report a failure, for `strategy = "minNumDown"`. Between 1 and 10.
- `strategy` (String) `noRecheck` concludes on the first failure, `fullAgreement` needs every location to agree, `downFullAgreement` needs full agreement only on the way down, `minNumDown` needs `min_num_down` locations to report a failure.


<a id="nestedatt--settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings`

Optional:

- `dnsbl` (Attributes) Settings for a standalone `dnsbl` monitor: look the host up in the DNS blacklists. It runs from a fixed internal network, so it takes no `locations`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--dnsbl))
- `domain_exp` (Attributes) Settings for a standalone `domainExp` monitor, which watches a registration's expiry. The API defines no members for it today. It runs from a fixed internal network, so it takes no `locations`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--domain_exp))
- `http` (Attributes) Settings for an `http` monitor: fetch a url and judge the answer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--http))
- `ping` (Attributes) Settings for a `ping` monitor: ICMP echo from the chosen locations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--ping))
- `port` (Attributes) Settings for a `port` monitor: open a TCP connection, optionally over TLS, and look at the banner. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--port))
- `ssl_exp` (Attributes) Settings for a standalone `sslExp` monitor, which watches a certificate's expiry. The API defines no members for it today; the block exists so that one it grows later is a plain attribute. It runs from a fixed internal network, so it takes no `locations`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--ssl_exp))
- `web_risk` (Attributes) Settings for a standalone `webRisk` monitor, which checks a url against Google's Web Risk lists. The API defines no members for it today. It runs from a fixed internal network, so it takes no `locations`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--web_risk))

<a id="nestedatt--settings--dnsbl"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings.dnsbl`

Optional:

- `scope` (String) Which addresses of the host are looked up: `firstWebIp` (the default), `allWebIps`, or `webAndMx`.


<a id="nestedatt--settings--domain_exp"></a>

<a id="nestedatt--settings--http"></a>
### Nested Schema for `settings.http`

Optional:

- `accept` (String) The Accept header to send.
- `assert_mode` (Boolean) Judge the response by the assertion list rather than by the keyword and status members, which are refused while it is on. Transport failures still fail the check either way.
- `asserts_source` (String) The assertion list as AssertRuleLang source text, one rule per line (`status eq 200`). It is parsed and stored as rows, so the API never reads it back: what is in the configuration stays in state. Read `asserts_text` for what the API actually stored.
- `attached` (Attributes) The sub-checks that run alongside this monitor's own check. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--http--attached))
- `auth_schema` (String) The authentication scheme. Only `Basic` is accepted.
- `block_weak_ciphers` (Boolean) Fail the check when the negotiated cipher suite is 128-bit or weaker.
- `body` (String) The raw request body.
- `cert_watch_days` (Set of Number) Days-before-expiry thresholds to alert on for the certificate this endpoint serves. At most 8 entries, each between 1 and 3650.
- `check_revocation` (Boolean) Fail the check when the certificate has been revoked, verified online during the handshake. Sold separately from the rest of the SSL policy.
- `dns` (Set of String) Resolver addresses to use instead of the monitoring location's own. At most 4.
- `dns_no_cache` (Boolean) Bypass the monitoring location's DNS cache.
- `error_on_redirect` (Boolean) Treat a 3xx as a failure.
- `error_statuses` (Set of Number) HTTP status codes that must fail the check. At most 20.
- `expected_dns` (Set of String) Resolver addresses the lookup is expected to come from. At most 10.
- `expected_ips` (Set of String) Addresses the host is expected to resolve to. Anything else fails the check. At most 10.
- `follow_redirect` (Boolean) Follow 3xx redirects. On by default.
- `headers` (Attributes List) Extra request headers, in order. Combined name and value length across all headers is capped at 1023 characters; `connection`, `content-length` and `date` are dropped. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--settings--http--headers))
- `ignored_statuses` (Set of Number) HTTP status codes that must not fail the check. At most 20.
- `keyword_mode` (String) How `keywords` decides the verdict: `PresentAny` (the default), `PresentAll`, `ReverseAny`, `ReverseAll`, `ReverseWithResult`. Read only when `keywords` is set.
- `keywords` (String) Comma-separated keywords matched against the response body. The whole list is capped at 255 characters.
- `max_redirects` (Number) How many redirect hops to follow. 20 is both the ceiling and the default.
- `max_size` (Number) The largest response body to download, in bytes.
- `method` (String) The HTTP method, as the single letter the executor takes: `G` (GET, the default), `H`, `P` (POST), `U` (PUT), `D` (DELETE), `A` (PATCH).
- `password` (String, Sensitive) HTTP basic auth password. Send it again to change it.
- `post_parameters` (String) Form-encoded POST parameters.
- `preset` (String) A server-built settings preset. `bl:ru` builds the whole settings object for a Russian-registry blacklist check and pins the monitoring locations.
- `public_dns` (Number) Run from public-DNS-filtered locations. `0` means the setting is not in force.
- `referer` (String) The Referer header to send.
- `require_strong_tls` (Boolean) Fail the check unless the connection negotiates TLS 1.2 or newer.
- `require_valid_chain` (Boolean) Fail the check unless the server presents a complete, trusted certificate chain. Off by default, which is why a self-signed certificate does not fail a check on its own.
- `timeout` (Number) Request timeout in milliseconds. 40000 by default, capped at 100000.
- `user_agent` (String) The User-Agent header to send.
- `username` (String) HTTP basic auth user name.

Read-Only:

- `asserts_text` (String) The stored assertion rows rendered back as source text. Written by the API from what `asserts_source` compiled to.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A monitor is imported by its id, which the web app shows in the address
# bar of the monitor's page and `hosttracker_monitors` publishes as `ids`.
terraform import hosttracker_monitor.marketing 8e2d4c8b-7a41-4a2b-9d0e-2f3a5c6b7d8e
```
